lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In two minutes, Dr. Vale will demonstrate an ancient torture machine on live television. He has rehearsed the screaming. He has not read the instructions. Mina has read them. That's why she's running.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two hours earlier, this was still supposed to be the greatest discovery of his career.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The year is three thousand twenty six. Under an old shopping center, Vale and Mina find a room full of heavy objects. There are handles to pull, platforms to push, and benches beneath enormous bars.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: A torture chamber.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Or a training room.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Training to do what? They lift the object, then put it exactly where it was.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He peers into a smaller room at the back. A desk. Two plastic chairs. A locked drawer.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: We'll examine that later.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He calls the museum. A banner goes up before the dust has settled. ANCIENT CRUELTY. LIVE DEMONSTRATION TODAY.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: We haven't finished looking.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Then look quickly.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mina restores a security recording. A man lies beneath a bar. His face tightens. Another man stands over him.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: One more.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: There. A confession.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: That's encouragement.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The bar returns to its supports. The two men laugh and shake hands.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Complicated society.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mina advances the recording. People enter through the front door. They leave through the same door. One comes back carrying special shoes.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: They can leave. They bring equipment. They appear to want to be here.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Play the part with the screaming again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Inside a locker, Mina finds a membership card and a receipt. Vale stops talking. He reads the payment. Then the renewal. Then the payment again.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: They paid?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Every month.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: For the suffering?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: For something. Let's find out what.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She turns the card over. There is a paragraph of tiny writing. Vale takes a photograph of the price and hurries away.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At the museum, his new headline is even larger. HUMANS PAID TO BE TORTURED.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: You found one new fact and made the conclusion worse.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mina follows the same member through recordings made weeks apart. On the first day, his coach removes weight from the bar. On a later day, the man completes that exercise more easily.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Watch him. Not the metal.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Vale watches. The bar is still a bar. The person handling it has improved.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: They were training.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Resistance makes muscles work against a load. Repeated training, with recovery, can make them stronger. As capacity improves, a suitable challenge can increase gradually. Progress takes time. It isn't one terrible afternoon.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Then why is there a heavier weight?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: A challenge that was hard can become easier. That doesn't mean everyone starts with the same one.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A different clip shows the coach stopping a painful movement and changing the exercise.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: And pain isn't the goal.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Vale retreats to his strongest evidence. A treadmill. He points at the recording of a woman walking on it.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Explain why they trapped her on a road.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: She controls the speed. She's exercising.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Brisk walking makes the heart beat faster and breathing work harder. Regular aerobic activity can improve fitness over time. Moving across a room isn't required for the body to be doing work.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: They invented vehicles to avoid walking. Then purchased walking?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: You're beginning to understand the species.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A museum assistant wheels the restored treadmill toward the demonstration stage. Vale follows it. Mina stays behind to finish reading the card.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Now the cameras are ready. The banner is enormous. Vale steps onto the stationary belt. He raises a solemn hand.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Today, I will experience what these people endured.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mina runs onto the stage.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Wait. You haven't attached the safety clip.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She shows him the stop control, attaches the clip, and starts the belt at a slow walking pace. Vale grips the rails, expecting catastrophe. He takes a step. Then another.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: When does the torture begin?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: It doesn't have to.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He lowers his prepared expression of agony. Behind him, his own headline fills the screen.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Then why not send a machine to lift the weights?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mina picks up a small demonstration weight. A museum robot takes it, lifts it, and returns it to the stand.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Did that train your muscles?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Vale looks at his arm. Then at the robot.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A machine can move a load for you. That doesn't give your muscles the training stimulus. Exercise asks your body to do the work so it can adapt over time.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: They weren't paying because the metal needed moving.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She puts the member's recordings on the screen. This time, she includes what happened outside the gym.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The man carries groceries up steps. The woman from the treadmill takes a walk with a friend. The coach holds the door while someone leaves, tired but laughing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Exercise can support everyday physical function. What people need, what they can do, and how they improve varies. A gym is one option. Home exercises and outdoor activity can count too.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: So they came here to make things outside this room easier.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Some did. And some probably just liked coming.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Vale looks from the ordinary lives on the screen to the sensational headline above him. The broadcast is still live. Vale reaches toward the broadcast control. He could stop the feed. Instead, he moves his hand to the treadmill's stop button.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: We need to change the sign.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Later, the new exhibit is almost ready. Vale has crossed out TORTURE CHAMBER and written GYM. Mina puts the membership card beside it.

lines.speaker: VALE
lines.text: Then what was in the little office?

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: Remember the tiny writing?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She restores one final recording. The member walks up to the office desk.

lines.speaker: MEMBER
lines.text: I'd like to cancel.

lines.speaker: CLERK
lines.text: Of course. Did you bring the form?

lines.speaker: MEMBER
lines.text: The one on the website?

lines.speaker: CLERK
lines.text: The one you request by mail.

lines.speaker: MEMBER
lines.text: Can I request it here?

lines.speaker: CLERK
lines.text: Online.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Vale slowly picks up his discarded sign.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On opening day, visitors pass the weights, the treadmill, and the recordings explaining how people trained. At the back is a reconstructed office. A desk. Two plastic chairs. A locked drawer.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Above its door, Vale has hung his original sign.

lines.speaker: MINA
lines.text: You finally found somewhere for it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In the end, Dr. Vale did discover a torture chamber. He'd just been pointing at the wrong room.
